advances.title: OpenAI mathematical research collection
advances.demonstrated: Published repository reports 721 manuscripts in 373 families; approximately 42% of top-line results formalized. This is evidence of accessible research artifacts, not a reproduced proof of every result.
advances.limitations: Mixed verification stages; an unnamed internal, unreleased model generated most results. Repository status and accepted scientific understanding are separate.
advances.availability: Public manuscript/proof artifacts; generating model not publicly established as available.
advances.study_access: Read README, history, formalization and comparator descriptions; did not compile full Lean corpus or claim independent validation.
advances.constraint_relaxed: Access to candidate mathematical constructions and some machine-checkable evidence.
advances.smallest_commercial_test: Choose a single relevant theorem, verify its exact hypotheses and proof status, implement its constructive content, then benchmark a paid-use outcome against an existing solver.
advances.excerpt: This collection includes results at different stages of verification.

advances.title: Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding
advances.demonstrated: OpenAI announced local smoothing/Kakeya, ETH-refutation and QCD-existence work. Math and computer-science artifacts were made public; physics release was deferred to an external collaboration.
advances.limitations: Manuscripts are characterized as raw research data. ETH's practical algorithmic consequences explicitly require further research; an asymptotic claim is not evidence of a faster commercial SAT solver.
advances.availability: Public math/CS artifacts; physics artifacts withheld; internal generating model.
advances.study_access: Announcement and public scope documentation read; no proof rerun, physics artifact access or new algorithm benchmark.
advances.constraint_relaxed: More candidates for mechanism discovery and independent scrutiny.
advances.smallest_commercial_test: Extract one concrete finite-instance algorithm and measure crossover with a mature free baseline before selling any improvement.
advances.excerpt: Finding such algorithms, and turning theoretical advances into practical improvements, will require significant further research.

advances.title: GPT-6.1 Terra and computer use
advances.demonstrated: Provider reports improved visual/computer-use performance, including 15 percentage points over GPT-5.6 Terra on Agents' Last Exam at medium effort and about one-third its task cost.
advances.limitations: Benchmark settings, task mix and production success differ. Published gains do not establish acceptance on this offering. Errors remain and verification must be charged.
advances.availability: Public ChatGPT Work/Codex and OpenAI API model gpt-6.1-terra.
advances.study_access: Listed in runtime catalog; not separately invoked or benchmarked in this workstream.
advances.constraint_relaxed: Cost and latency of visual interpretation and routine tool operation.
advances.smallest_commercial_test: Route repeated low-risk extraction/operation tasks to Terra under the same acceptance checker; compare accepted-outcome cost, escalation and repair with Astra.

advances.title: GPT-6 Astra
advances.demonstrated: Provider reports strong reasoning, scientific coding and computer use. Astra supports multistep work across tools; official API changelog verifies the September 3 release.
advances.limitations: Research evaluations can differ from production ChatGPT because of prompts, tools and safeguards. Benchmark performance cannot stand in for domain acceptance or human equivalence.
advances.availability: Public paid ChatGPT plans and API gpt-6-astra; enterprise enablement and product conditions apply.
advances.study_access: Session authoring/research and tool orchestration; no exposed immutable model checkpoint or measured token invoice.
advances.constraint_relaxed: Construction and debugging of missing domain tools within a bounded campaign.
advances.smallest_commercial_test: Require an executable deliverable and independent verifier; compare against a competent AI-assisted engineer using the same free tools.

advances.title: AlphaEvolve commercial and scientific applications
advances.demonstrated: Google reports evaluator-driven algorithm search across scientific and infrastructure workloads, including AC-OPF feasibility, hardware design and commercial computational lithography.
advances.limitations: Reported results are workload-specific and were not reproduced here. AlphaEvolve service access and commercial terms are not established in this study.
advances.availability: Public descriptions and selected artifacts; Google Cloud commercialization reported, not equivalent to study entitlement.
advances.constraint_relaxed: Evidence that agent-created algorithms can produce useful domain improvements when paired with executable evaluation.
advances.smallest_commercial_test: Build a bounded search with independent held-out evaluation; compare to ordinary optimization, search and skilled current-AI use.

advances.title: Claude Opus 5.5
advances.demonstrated: Anthropic reports improvements in coding, computer use and professional work, alongside lower typical task cost than Opus 5.
advances.limitations: Provider notes benchmark margins can be poor guides to real-world differences. This campaign has not run Claude; cannot claim Astra or an enterprise-specific routing system beats it.
advances.availability: Public product/API release; some biology/cyber workflows use verified-access programs.
advances.study_access: Primary documentation only; no credentials or model invocation.
advances.constraint_relaxed: Competitors and buyers also gain cheaper capable AI.
advances.smallest_commercial_test: Include competent competitor delivery and falling rival costs in economics; a head-to-head model test requires separate access.

advances.title: OpenEvolve open-source evolutionary coding
advances.demonstrated: Public evolutionary coding framework uses candidate generation and task evaluators; current commit rejects non-finite outputs in selected evaluators.
advances.limitations: Framework availability is not free inference, correct evaluation, or proof of commercial advantage. Evaluator errors and overfitting remain material.
advances.availability: Apache-2.0 source; depends on chosen model and execution resources.
advances.study_access: Repository and current commit inspected, not installed or used for construction.
advances.constraint_relaxed: A conventional team can obtain automated code search without inventing a proprietary agent framework.
advances.smallest_commercial_test: Use as a practical search baseline or reproduce equivalent bounded generate-test-select procedure with identical budget and untouched holdout.

advances.title: DeepSeek-Prover-V2
advances.demonstrated: Open proof models combine informal decomposition and Lean proof search. The paper reports benchmark gains and releases 7B/671B versions.
advances.limitations: Historical enabling baseline, not a new October 2026 release. Formal proofs establish encoded statements only; domain modeling and economic value remain separate.
advances.availability: Public code/weights and papers; compute required.
advances.study_access: Paper and repository read; weights not downloaded or run.
advances.constraint_relaxed: Independent formal-checking approaches need not rely on the newest proprietary model.
advances.smallest_commercial_test: Verify a small domain invariant with an available checker, then test whether formalization cost is justified by buyer requirements.

advances.title: HiGHS and SciPy MILP as free competent alternatives
advances.date_basis: Current documentation checked; not claimed as a newly released method.
advances.demonstrated: HiGHS provides LP/MIP/QP solvers under MIT license; SciPy exposes deterministic MILP solving with explicit status, bounds and gaps.
advances.limitations: A solver guarantees only the posed model within numerical tolerances; it does not validate physics, demand or omitted constraints.
advances.availability: Free source; SciPy installed in local environment.
advances.study_access: Documentation read and SciPy availability confirmed; exact experiment runtime version should be recorded by construction workstream.
advances.constraint_relaxed: Sophisticated conventional decision algorithms are available at negligible license cost.
advances.smallest_commercial_test: Implement the strongest correct mathematical formulation as baseline; compare outcome acceptance and total engineering/delivery cost.

preserved_failure.finding: October 7 history records three withdrawn manuscripts after a sign error, 14 manuscript revisions and updates to dependent citations. October 26 includes comparator fixes. This motivates exact-version, dependency and failure preservation.
preserved_failure.excluded_claim: No proof or advertised scientific discovery was independently reproduced by this source investigation.

routing_hypothesis.formula: Expected accepted-outcome cost = (routine model cost + escalation probability * specialist cost + verification + repair + human exceptions) / acceptance probability.
routing_hypothesis.illustration: At published standard prices, 100,000 uncached input plus 20,000 output tokens cost $0.20 on Terra or $2.00 on Astra, excluding tools, retries and verification. These are arithmetic examples, not measured workloads or invoices.
routing_hypothesis.operating_stack: Deterministic parsing/solvers/checkers first; low-cost model for bounded extraction and routine operation; specialist model for ambiguous construction and repair; independent acceptance checks; human review at domain and commercial authority boundaries.
routing_hypothesis.test_required: Randomized comparable tasks with token/latency/error metering before adopting routing savings. No future model improvement is required for the current commercial base case.

frontier_crossing: Previously, tailored domain constructions could be dominated by expensive translation, implementation and checking. Recent public models lower the cost of tool construction and operation; free verifiers/solvers supply strong checks. The missing means is a domain-specific representation, executable acceptance contract and complete delivery process. The new commercial outcome must be measured at that boundary; a recent announcement alone does not prove the outcome was previously impossible.
